problem: The first accountant evaluation completed the workflow but found contradictory next-step instructions after both original approvals: reviewer guidance still requested approvals despite Ready to pay and 2 of 2. Related findings KONTOR-ACCOUNTANT-R1-02 through 05 identify the same stale imperative after revised approval, missing adjacent credit-role guidance, ambiguous historical approval status and an unlabeled JSON export format. Findings are controller-attested mappings of the unchanged accountant-round1.json observations; this proposal does not claim technically enforced blindness.
userImpact: An accountant can repeat completed review work or doubt payment readiness, must remember which demo actor may apply a credit, and must infer historical approval expiry and export format. The financial workflow completed successfully; the improvement targets clarity and handoff confidence without changing authorization or settlement behavior.
proposedChange: Derive visible instructions from the authoritative current approval set and status. With two current approvals, reviewer/approver guidance says Both approvals are recorded and names the payment operator; with zero or one it identifies remaining review work. After a credit, show Approve the revised amount only while approvals remain incomplete; once approved show Revised [amount] Test USD approved. Ready for payment. Beside a disabled credit control, name the reviewer authorized to use it. In displayed historical approval evidence, label approvals from an earlier revision Expired after [credit reference] and show Invoice version [revision], preserving original record text and export data. Label the existing download Export evidence (JSON). Scope is presentation-only within src/App.tsx and, only if needed, src/styles.css.
acceptanceCriteria: At original 1,000 Test USD with two current approvals, the reviewer sees completed-approval guidance and the named payment operator; no visible instruction asks for two approvals again. Credit remains available to the reviewer before payment.

At revised 800 Test USD with zero or one current approval, guidance asks only for remaining approvals. At two current approvals, the callout says the revised amount is approved and ready for payment; no visible callout asks to approve 800 again.
When credit is available but disabled for a non-reviewer actor, adjacent readable text names the reviewer and their role. This guidance is available without hover on both desktop and 390 px width.

Original approval events after a credit explicitly show expiry after the actual credit-note reference and their invoice version. Current approval events remain distinguishable; underlying immutable evidence and downloaded data are unchanged.
The existing download control identifies JSON. No new file format, accounting certification claim, notification workflow, role permission, API, or payment operation is introduced.

Typecheck and production build pass. A fresh-context accountant regression checks 0/2, 1/2 and 2/2 guidance before and after credit, historical versus current evidence, export labeling, and completion through one 800 Test USD payment at desktop and narrow width. Integration verification remains separate from browser usability evidence.
tradeoffs: A small amount of contextual help is added beside the disabled credit control; this increases rail height slightly but removes dependence on hover and memory.

Historical evidence receives a derived display annotation while original record text remains unchanged. It must use the event revision and actual credit reference, never infer expiry merely from an amount difference.
JSON remains the sole export format. A printable accounting summary is deferred because it would expand this bounded copy and handoff improvement.
This fixes observed copy contradictions rather than claiming a comprehensive accessibility audit or stronger browser isolation.
